category: .NET API: Editor Input, Transactions, Symbol Tables & Data Storage
description: The AutoCAD managed .NET API (AcMgd.dll, AcDbMgd.dll, AcCoreMgd.dll; .NET 8 from AutoCAD 2025, .NET Framework 4.8 before): Editor prompts and selection, SelectionFilter/TypedValue/ResultBuffer, document locking and command execution, the transaction pattern, symbol tables, ObjectId/Handle, XData, Xrecords and dictionaries, extension-application entry points, autoloader bundles and side-database operations. Not available in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: Editor.GetSelection
tools.description: Prompts the user to select objects and returns a PromptSelectionResult whose Value is a SelectionSet. Overloads accept PromptSelectionOptions (custom prompts, single-only, keywords) and a SelectionFilter that restricts which objects can be selected, like ssget with a filter list.
tools.usage:
PromptSelectionResult Editor.GetSelection()
PromptSelectionResult Editor.GetSelection(SelectionFilter filter)
PromptSelectionResult Editor.GetSelection(PromptSelectionOptions options, SelectionFilter filter)

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: PromptSelectionOptions: MessageForAdding, MessageForRemoval, SingleOnly, SinglePickInSpace, RejectObjectsOnLockedLayers, Keywords.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: SelectionFilter built from TypedValue pairs (DXF codes).

parameters.name: result.Status
parameters.description: PromptStatus.OK when something was selected; Cancel or Error otherwise.

tools.notes: The objects are returned as ObjectIds; open them inside a transaction. Must run in document context (a command without CommandFlags.Session) or the prompt fails.

tools.name: Editor.SelectAll
tools.description: Selects all objects in the drawing database that pass an optional SelectionFilter, without user interaction. Equivalent to (ssget "_X" filter) and includes objects in model space and all paper-space layouts.
tools.usage:
PromptSelectionResult Editor.SelectAll()
PromptSelectionResult Editor.SelectAll(SelectionFilter filter)

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Optional SelectionFilter; add (410, "Model") to restrict to model space.

tools.notes: Status is Error (not OK) when nothing matches, so check the status before using Value. Iterating BlockTableRecord contents is an alternative when you need a single space only.

tools.name: Editor.SelectImplied
tools.description: Returns the pickfirst (noun-verb) selection set, i.e. objects the user selected before starting the command. SetImpliedSelection does the reverse and highlights a set of ObjectIds as the current pickfirst set.
tools.usage:
PromptSelectionResult Editor.SelectImplied()
void Editor.SetImpliedSelection(ObjectId[] ids)

parameters.name: CommandFlags.UsePickSet
parameters.description: The command must be declared with UsePickSet or the pickfirst set is cleared before it runs.

parameters.name: CommandFlags.Redraw
parameters.description: Needed on the command for SetImpliedSelection results to remain selected after the command ends.

tools.notes: Fall back to GetSelection when the implied set is empty (Status != OK). SetImpliedSelection is how 'select similar' style tools hand back a selection.

tools.name: Editor.GetEntity
tools.description: Prompts the user to pick a single object and returns its ObjectId and the pick point. PromptEntityOptions can restrict the allowed classes (for example only Polyline) with a rejection message, and allow keywords or Enter.
tools.usage:
PromptEntityResult Editor.GetEntity(PromptEntityOptions options)
PromptEntityResult Editor.GetEntity(string message)

parameters.name: SetRejectMessage
parameters.description: Message shown when a disallowed class is picked; must be called before AddAllowedClass.

parameters.name: AddAllowedClass(Type, bool exactMatch)
parameters.description: Allowed entity type; exactMatch false also accepts derived classes.

parameters.name: result.ObjectId / PickedPoint
parameters.description: Selected object and the UCS pick point.

tools.notes: Calling AddAllowedClass before SetRejectMessage throws an exception. For objects inside blocks or xrefs use GetNestedEntity.

tools.name: Editor.GetNestedEntity
tools.description: Lets the user pick an entity nested inside a block reference or xref and returns its ObjectId together with the transformation matrix to WCS and the chain of containing block references. The .NET counterpart of nentsel/nentselp.
tools.usage: PromptNestedEntityResult Editor.GetNestedEntity(PromptNestedEntityOptions options)

parameters.name: result.ObjectId
parameters.description: The nested entity (in the block definition's database).

parameters.name: result.Transform
parameters.description: Matrix3d from block-definition coordinates to WCS.

parameters.name: result.GetContainers()
parameters.description: ObjectIds of the containing block references, innermost first.

tools.notes: For xrefs the ObjectId belongs to the xref database, which is read-only in the host drawing.

tools.name: Editor.GetPoint
tools.description: Prompts for a point, with optional rubber-band line from a base point, keywords and Enter-to-accept behaviour. The result is expressed in the current UCS and must be transformed to WCS before being used to create entities.
tools.usage:
PromptPointResult Editor.GetPoint(PromptPointOptions options)
PromptPointResult Editor.GetPoint(string message)

parameters.name: UseBasePoint / BasePoint
parameters.description: Draws a rubber-band line from BasePoint (UCS).

parameters.name: AllowNone
parameters.description: true lets the user press Enter (Status = None).

parameters.name: Keywords
parameters.description: Optional keywords; Status = Keyword with StringResult set.

tools.notes: GetCorner draws a rectangle from a base point instead of a line. Object snaps and tracking apply automatically.

tools.name: Editor.GetKeywords
tools.description: Prompts the user to choose one of a set of keywords, shown as clickable command-line options, with an optional default. The chosen global keyword is returned in StringResult.
tools.usage: PromptResult Editor.GetKeywords(PromptKeywordOptions options)

parameters.name: Keywords.Add(global, local, display)
parameters.description: Adds a keyword; the capital letters define the shortcut.

parameters.name: Keywords.Default
parameters.description: Keyword returned when the user presses Enter.

parameters.name: AllowNone
parameters.description: Allow Enter when no default is set.

tools.notes: Other prompt option classes (PromptPointOptions, PromptEntityOptions, PromptSelectionOptions) also carry Keywords; they then return Status = Keyword.

tools.name: Editor.GetString
tools.description: Prompts for a text string on the command line. With AllowSpaces the user can type spaces, and Enter ends input; otherwise a space also terminates the entry.
tools.usage:
PromptResult Editor.GetString(PromptStringOptions options)
PromptResult Editor.GetString(string message)

parameters.name: AllowSpaces
parameters.description: true to accept spaces in the string.

parameters.name: DefaultValue / UseDefaultValue
parameters.description: Value returned when the user just presses Enter.

tools.notes: Validate names destined for symbol tables with SymbolUtilityServices.ValidateSymbolName, which throws for invalid characters.

tools.name: Editor.GetDouble
tools.description: Prompts for a real number with validation options for zero, negative values and a default. Companion methods GetInteger, GetDistance (accepts two picked points) and GetAngle (accepts picks, returns radians) follow the same pattern.
tools.usage:
PromptDoubleResult Editor.GetDouble(PromptDoubleOptions options)
PromptIntegerResult Editor.GetInteger(PromptIntegerOptions options)
PromptDoubleResult Editor.GetDistance(PromptDistanceOptions options)

parameters.name: AllowNegative / AllowZero
parameters.description: Input validation switches (default: both allowed).

parameters.name: DefaultValue / UseDefaultValue
parameters.description: Value used when the user presses Enter.

parameters.name: LowerLimit / UpperLimit
parameters.description: Range limits for PromptIntegerOptions.

tools.notes: GetDistance honours the current linear units format for typed input (feet-inches etc.), unlike GetDouble.

tools.name: Editor.WriteMessage
tools.description: Writes text to the command-line window, with composite-format support like String.Format. It is the standard way to report results and progress from a command.
tools.usage:
void Editor.WriteMessage(string message)
void Editor.WriteMessage(string format, params object[] args)

parameters.name: message / format
parameters.description: Text; start with \n to begin on a new line.

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: Values substituted into {0}, {1} ... placeholders.

tools.example: ed.WriteMessage("\nProcessed {0} drawings in {1:F1} s.", count, sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds);
tools.notes: Curly braces in a literal message passed to the params overload must be doubled. In accoreconsole the output goes to stdout, which is useful for batch logging.

tools.name: Editor.Command
tools.description: Executes AutoCAD commands synchronously from a .NET command, like (command-s) in AutoLISP: the arguments are passed in sequence and the call returns when the command sequence completes. Available since AutoCAD 2015.
tools.usage: void Editor.Command(params object[] parameters)

parameters.name: parameters
parameters.description: Command names and inputs: strings, numbers, Point3d, ObjectId, SelectionSet; "" is Enter.

tools.notes: Only valid in document context; from a session-context command or a modeless UI use Document.SendStringToExecute. The sequence must be complete; use Editor.CommandAsync when the user must interact (pause).

tools.name: Editor.CommandAsync
tools.description: Asynchronous counterpart of Editor.Command that can pause for user input with Editor.PauseToken. It returns an awaitable object, so the calling command method is declared async and awaits each step.
tools.usage:
Editor.CommandResult Editor.CommandAsync(params object[] parameters)
await ed.CommandAsync("_.LINE", Editor.PauseToken, Editor.PauseToken, "");

parameters.name: Editor.PauseToken
parameters.description: Placeholder that lets the user supply that input interactively.

parameters.name: parameters
parameters.description: Same types as Editor.Command.

tools.notes: Use async void only for CommandMethod handlers. Exceptions thrown after an await are reported differently; wrap the body in try/catch.

tools.name: Editor.CurrentUserCoordinateSystem
tools.description: Gets or sets the current UCS as a Matrix3d that transforms UCS coordinates to WCS. Points returned by prompts are in UCS and must be transformed with this matrix before creating geometry in the database, which always stores WCS (or OCS) values.
tools.usage: Matrix3d Editor.CurrentUserCoordinateSystem { get; set; }

parameters.name: get
parameters.description: UCS-to-WCS matrix; use .Inverse() for WCS-to-UCS.

parameters.name: set
parameters.description: Assign a matrix built with Matrix3d.AlignCoordinateSystem to change the UCS.

tools.notes: Forgetting the UCS transform is the most common bug in .NET drawing code; it only shows up when the user works in a rotated UCS.

tools.name: SelectionFilter
tools.description: Filter used by Editor.GetSelection and SelectAll, constructed from an array of TypedValue pairs using DXF group codes, including relational and logical operators (-4). It mirrors the AutoLISP ssget filter-list syntax.
tools.usage: new SelectionFilter(TypedValue[] values)

parameters.name: DxfCode.Start (0)
parameters.description: Object type, wildcards allowed: "LINE,ARC,*POLYLINE".

parameters.name: DxfCode.LayerName (8)
parameters.description: Layer name with wildcards.

parameters.name: DxfCode.Operator (-4)
parameters.description: "<OR" ... "OR>", "<AND", "<NOT", "<XOR" and relational tests "<", ">=", "*".

tools.example:
var f = new SelectionFilter(new[] {
    new TypedValue(-4, "<OR"),
      new TypedValue(0, "LINE"),
      new TypedValue(-4, "<AND"),
        new TypedValue(0, "LWPOLYLINE"), new TypedValue(70, 1),
      new TypedValue(-4, "AND>"),
    new TypedValue(-4, "OR>") });
tools.notes: Bit-coded flags such as 70 need the "&" or "&=" relational operator to test bits. Filtering on properties that are ByLayer (color 256) does not match the layer's color.

tools.name: TypedValue
tools.description: An immutable pair of a DXF type code and a value, the .NET equivalent of an AutoLISP dotted pair. It is the element type of selection filters, ResultBuffers (XData, Xrecord data, LISP arguments) and several other APIs.
tools.usage:
new TypedValue(int typeCode, object value)
tv.TypeCode  tv.Value

parameters.name: typeCode
parameters.description: DXF group code, usually cast from the DxfCode or LispDataType enum.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Value whose .NET type matches the code (string, short, int, double, Point3d, ObjectId...).

tools.example:
var tv = new TypedValue((int)DxfCode.ExtendedDataReal, 3.5);
if (tv.TypeCode == 1040) ed.WriteMessage($"\nReal xdata: {(double)tv.Value}");
tools.notes: Using the wrong .NET type for a code (for example int instead of short for 70) causes eInvalidResBuf or silent filter mismatches.

tools.name: ResultBuffer
tools.description: A disposable list of TypedValue items, the managed wrapper of the ObjectARX resbuf chain. It carries XData, Xrecord data, arguments and return values of [LispFunction] methods, and data for Application.Invoke.
tools.usage:
new ResultBuffer(params TypedValue[] values)
rb.Add(TypedValue)  rb.AsArray()  foreach (TypedValue tv in rb)

parameters.name: AsArray()
parameters.description: Returns the items as TypedValue[].

parameters.name: Dispose()
parameters.description: Release native memory; use a using statement.

tools.notes: LISP arguments use LispDataType codes (Int16 5003, Double 5001, Text 5005, Point3d 5009, ListBegin 5016...), not DXF codes.

tools.name: PromptStatus
tools.description: Enumeration returned in the Status property of every prompt result, telling whether the user supplied a value, cancelled, pressed Enter or chose a keyword. Every prompt call should branch on it before reading Value.
tools.usage: PromptStatus.OK | Cancel | None | Keyword | Error | Modeless | Other

parameters.name: OK
parameters.description: A valid value was entered.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: User pressed Esc.

parameters.name: None
parameters.description: Enter pressed with AllowNone = true.

parameters.name: Keyword
parameters.description: A keyword was chosen; read StringResult.

tools.notes: Reading Value when Status is not OK returns a default value (for example Point3d.Origin), which silently produces wrong geometry.

tools.name: Document.LockDocument
tools.description: Locks a document for writing and returns a DocumentLock that releases the lock when disposed. Required whenever the database is modified from application (session) context: modeless dialogs, palettes, ribbon handlers, event handlers and commands registered with CommandFlags.Session.
tools.usage: using (DocumentLock loc = doc.LockDocument()) { ... }

parameters.name: overloads
parameters.description: LockDocument(DocumentLockMode mode, string globalCommandName, string localCommandName, bool promptIfFails) for explicit lock modes.

tools.notes: Missing locks produce eLockViolation. Ordinary modal commands run in document context and already hold the lock.

tools.name: Document.SendStringToExecute
tools.description: Queues a command string to be executed asynchronously in a document when AutoCAD becomes idle, as if typed at the command line. It is the reliable way to start commands from modeless UI, from session-context code or in another document.
tools.usage: void Document.SendStringToExecute(string command, bool activate, bool wrapUpInactiveDoc, bool echoCommand)

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: Command text; end with a space or \n to press Enter.

parameters.name: activate
parameters.description: true activates the target document first.

parameters.name: wrapUpInactiveDoc
parameters.description: true to finish execution in an inactive document (used when switching documents).

parameters.name: echoCommand
parameters.description: true echoes the command on the command line.

tools.notes: The string runs after the current command finishes, so code after the call cannot rely on its effects. Prefer Editor.Command inside document-context commands.

tools.name: DocumentCollection.Open
tools.description: Opens a drawing file in the editor and returns its Document. Since AutoCAD 2015 Open and Add (new drawing from template) are extension methods in DocumentCollectionExtension, called on Application.DocumentManager.
tools.usage:
Document DocumentCollectionExtension.Open(this DocumentCollection docs, string fileName, bool forReadOnly, string password)
Document DocumentCollectionExtension.Add(this DocumentCollection docs, string templateFileName)

parameters.name: fileName
parameters.description: Full DWG path.

parameters.name: forReadOnly
parameters.description: true to open read-only.

parameters.name: templateFileName
parameters.description: DWT used by Add.

tools.notes: Must be called from session context (CommandFlags.Session or modeless UI), because opening switches documents. For batch reading without the editor, use Database.ReadDwgFile instead.

tools.name: Application.GetSystemVariable
tools.description: Reads a system variable and returns it as object; Application.SetSystemVariable writes one. The static methods live on Autodesk.AutoCAD.ApplicationServices.Application and act on the current document for drawing-level variables.
tools.usage:
object Application.GetSystemVariable(string name)
void Application.SetSystemVariable(string name, object value)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: System variable name, case-insensitive.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: New value; pass the variable's own type (integers are typically Int16, reals double, points Point3d).

tools.notes: Always restore changed variables in a finally block. Some variables are available directly as Database properties (db.Clayer, db.Ltscale), which also works on side databases.

tools.name: Application.ShowAlertDialog
tools.description: Displays a simple modal message box with an OK button, parented to the AutoCAD main window. Equivalent to AutoLISP (alert).
tools.usage: void Application.ShowAlertDialog(string message)

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Text to display.

tools.example: Application.ShowAlertDialog($"Export finished:\n{outputPath}");
tools.notes: Blocks the UI; in batch or accoreconsole use Editor.WriteMessage instead. For richer dialogs use Application.ShowModalDialog with a WinForms/WPF window.

tools.name: Transaction.GetObject
tools.description: Opens a database object by ObjectId within a transaction and returns it as DBObject, which is then cast to the specific type. The object remains open until the transaction ends, and all objects are closed automatically on Commit or Dispose.
tools.usage:
DBObject Transaction.GetObject(ObjectId id, OpenMode mode)
DBObject Transaction.GetObject(ObjectId id, OpenMode mode, bool openErased, bool forceOpenOnLockedLayer)

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ObjectId of the object.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: OpenMode.ForRead, ForWrite or ForNotify.

parameters.name: openErased
parameters.description: true to open erased objects (e.g. to unerase).

parameters.name: forceOpenOnLockedLayer
parameters.description: true to open entities on locked layers for write.

tools.notes: Open for read first and call UpgradeOpen() only on objects you change; opening everything for write is slower and fails on locked layers (eOnLockedLayer). Pattern matching (is Circle c) or 'as' casts avoid InvalidCastException when iterating mixed entities.

tools.name: OpenMode
tools.description: Enumeration that states how a database object is opened: ForRead (many readers allowed), ForWrite (exclusive, required to modify) or ForNotify (used by reactors/overrules). DBObject.UpgradeOpen and DowngradeOpen switch between read and write on an open object.
tools.usage: OpenMode.ForRead | OpenMode.ForWrite | OpenMode.ForNotify

parameters.name: ForRead
parameters.description: Read-only access; modifying throws eNotOpenForWrite.

parameters.name: ForWrite
parameters.description: Write access; fails for objects on locked layers unless forced.

parameters.name: ForNotify
parameters.description: Notification access used internally by reactors.

tools.example:
var ent = (Entity)tr.GetObject(id, OpenMode.ForRead);
if (ent.Layer == "TEMP") { ent.UpgradeOpen(); ent.Erase(); }
tools.notes: Symbol tables (LayerTable, BlockTable) need ForWrite only when adding records: call UpgradeOpen just before Add.

tools.name: Transaction.AddNewlyCreatedDBObject
tools.description: Registers a newly created object with the transaction after it has been added to the database (AppendEntity, SymbolTable.Add, DBDictionary.SetAt). The transaction then manages closing it, and aborting the transaction removes it again.
tools.usage: void Transaction.AddNewlyCreatedDBObject(DBObject obj, bool add)

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: The new object, already database-resident.

parameters.name: add
parameters.description: true to add to the transaction (normal case).

tools.notes: Forgetting this call leaves the new object open, producing eWasOpenForWrite errors or a crash on exit. Call it after AppendEntity/Add, not before.

tools.name: Transaction.Commit
tools.description: Commits all changes made in the transaction and closes every object opened through it. Disposing a transaction without committing aborts it and rolls back all changes, which is the built-in error recovery of the pattern.
tools.usage:
void Transaction.Commit()
void Transaction.Abort()

parameters.name: Abort()
parameters.description: Explicitly roll back; Dispose without Commit does the same.

tools.notes: Commit even read-only transactions: aborting is more expensive than committing. Nested transactions must be committed or aborted innermost first.

tools.name: StartOpenCloseTransaction
tools.description: Starts an OpenCloseTransaction, a lightweight transaction that uses the classic open/close mechanism internally instead of the transaction manager. It is safe to use inside event handlers, overrules and jigs where a regular transaction could interfere with the one the command is running.
tools.usage: OpenCloseTransaction TransactionManager.StartOpenCloseTransaction()

parameters.name: return value
parameters.description: An OpenCloseTransaction with the same GetObject/AddNewlyCreatedDBObject/Commit API.

tools.notes: It does not support nesting semantics or undo-grouping like the regular transaction manager, but it is faster for many small read operations.

tools.name: BlockTableRecord.AppendEntity
tools.description: Adds a new entity to a block table record (model space, a paper-space layout or a block definition) and returns its ObjectId. The record must be open for write, and the entity must then be registered with the transaction.
tools.usage: ObjectId BlockTableRecord.AppendEntity(Entity entity)

parameters.name: entity
parameters.description: A new, non-database-resident Entity.

tools.notes: db.CurrentSpaceId targets whatever space is active; SymbolUtilityServices.GetBlockModelSpaceId(db) always returns model space. Call SetDatabaseDefaults to pick up current layer, color and linetype.

tools.name: LayerTableRecord
tools.description: A layer definition in the LayerTable, with Name, Color, LinetypeObjectId, LineWeight, IsFrozen, IsOff, IsLocked, IsPlottable and Transparency. Layers are created by adding a new record to the LayerTable and modified by opening existing records for write.
tools.usage:
var ltr = new LayerTableRecord { Name = "E-POWER", Color = Color.FromColorIndex(ColorMethod.ByAci, 1) };
layerTable.Add(ltr); tr.AddNewlyCreatedDBObject(ltr, true);

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Layer name (validate with SymbolUtilityServices.ValidateSymbolName).

parameters.name: IsFrozen / IsOff / IsLocked
parameters.description: Visibility and edit state; the current layer cannot be frozen.

parameters.name: LinetypeObjectId
parameters.description: ObjectId of a LinetypeTableRecord (must be loaded).

tools.notes: Changing IsFrozen on layers needs a Regen (ed.Regen()) to update the display. Viewport-specific freezing uses Viewport.FreezeLayersInViewport.

tools.name: SymbolTable.Has
tools.description: Tests whether a symbol table (LayerTable, BlockTable, TextStyleTable, LinetypeTable, DimStyleTable, RegAppTable, UcsTable, ViewTable) contains a record with a given name or ObjectId. The string indexer then returns the record's ObjectId.
tools.usage:
bool SymbolTable.Has(string key)
bool SymbolTable.Has(ObjectId id)
ObjectId SymbolTable[string key]

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Record name, case-insensitive.

tools.example:
var bt = (BlockTable)tr.GetObject(db.BlockTableId, OpenMode.ForRead);
ObjectId blkId = bt.Has("TITLE_A1") ? bt["TITLE_A1"] : ImportBlock(db, "TITLE_A1");
tools.notes: Has returns true for erased records in some releases; check !id.IsErased when it matters. The indexer throws if the name is missing.

tools.name: Database.LoadLineTypeFile
tools.description: Loads one or more linetype definitions (wildcards allowed) from a .lin file into the database's LinetypeTable, so they can be assigned to layers or entities.
tools.usage: void Database.LoadLineTypeFile(string linetypeName, string filename)

parameters.name: linetypeName
parameters.description: Linetype name or wildcard pattern, e.g. "DASHED" or "*".

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: "acad.lin", "acadiso.lin" or a full path; found on the support path.

tools.notes: Loading a linetype that already exists throws eDuplicateRecordName; check Has first. Linetypes referencing shapes need the corresponding .shx on the support path.

tools.name: ObjectId
tools.description: Session-level identifier of a database-resident object, used to open objects in transactions and to link objects. Its ObjectClass property exposes the runtime class without opening the object, which enables very fast type filtering over large collections.
tools.usage: ObjectId id;  id.IsNull  id.IsErased  id.IsValid  id.ObjectClass  id.Database  id.Handle

parameters.name: ObjectClass
parameters.description: RXClass; compare DxfName or use IsDerivedFrom(RXObject.GetClass(typeof(Curve))).

parameters.name: IsNull / IsErased
parameters.description: Validity checks before opening.

parameters.name: Handle
parameters.description: The persistent Handle of the object.

tools.notes: ObjectIds change between sessions; store Handles (or use the object's persistent reference) when you need identity across saves.

tools.name: Handle
tools.description: The persistent hexadecimal identifier of an object (DXF group code 5), stable across save and reopen. Database.GetObjectId or TryGetObjectId converts a handle back to an ObjectId in the current session.

parameters.name: createIfNotFound
parameters.description: GetObjectId first argument; normally false.

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description: Reserved; pass 0.

tools.notes: Handles are unique only within one drawing; copying objects to another drawing assigns new handles.

tools.name: DBObject.XData
tools.description: Gets or sets the extended entity data (XData) of an object as a ResultBuffer. Each application's data starts with a 1001 registered-application name that must exist in the RegAppTable. GetXDataForApplication reads one application's block.
tools.usage:
ResultBuffer DBObject.XData { get; set; }
ResultBuffer DBObject.GetXDataForApplication(string regAppName)

parameters.description: Registered application name (DxfCode.ExtendedDataRegAppName).
String, real, 16-bit integer and 32-bit integer values.
Database handle that is translated on copy (soft pointer).

tools.notes: Setting XData for one application leaves other applications' XData untouched. Total XData per object is limited to about 16 KB; store larger data in an extension dictionary Xrecord.

tools.name: Xrecord
tools.description: A non-graphical object that stores arbitrary data as a ResultBuffer (Data property) inside a DBDictionary, either the named objects dictionary or an object's extension dictionary. Xrecords have no size limit comparable to XData and are the preferred way to store application data in drawings.
tools.usage:
var xr = new Xrecord { Data = new ResultBuffer(...) };
dict.SetAt("KEY", xr); tr.AddNewlyCreatedDBObject(xr, true);

parameters.name: Data
parameters.description: ResultBuffer using ordinary DXF codes (1-369, not 1000+ XData codes).

parameters.name: XlateReferences
parameters.description: Whether handle references in the data are translated on deep clone.

tools.notes: Readable from AutoLISP with dictsearch/entget, so data can be shared between LISP and .NET.

tools.name: DBDictionary
tools.description: A container object mapping string keys to ObjectIds of other objects (Xrecords, nested dictionaries, layouts, groups, styles). It is enumerable as DBDictionaryEntry (Key, Value) pairs and provides Contains, GetAt, SetAt and Remove.
tools.usage: bool Contains(string key)  ObjectId GetAt(string key)  ObjectId SetAt(string key, DBObject obj)  void Remove(string key)

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Entry name (case-insensitive, unique within the dictionary).

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: New object to add; must then be added to the transaction.

tools.notes: Built-in dictionaries in the NOD include ACAD_GROUP, ACAD_LAYOUT, ACAD_MLINESTYLE, ACAD_MLEADERSTYLE, ACAD_TABLESTYLE, ACAD_PLOTSETTINGS, ACAD_MATERIAL and ACAD_VISUALSTYLE.

tools.name: Database.NamedObjectsDictionaryId
tools.description: ObjectId of the drawing's named objects dictionary (NOD), the root dictionary for drawing-wide non-graphical data such as groups, layouts, styles and application-defined Xrecords.
tools.usage: ObjectId Database.NamedObjectsDictionaryId { get; }

parameters.name: return value
parameters.description: Open it as DBDictionary; ForWrite to add entries.

tools.example:
var nod = (DBDictionary)tr.GetObject(db.NamedObjectsDictionaryId, OpenMode.ForRead);
bool hasMyData = nod.Contains("ACME_SETTINGS");
tools.notes: Prefix your own keys with a registered developer symbol to avoid collisions with other applications. The AutoLISP equivalent is (namedobjdict).

tools.name: DBObject.CreateExtensionDictionary
tools.description: Creates an extension dictionary owned by an object, after which the ExtensionDictionary property returns its ObjectId. Extension dictionaries hold per-object Xrecords and are copied and erased along with the owner.
tools.usage:
void DBObject.CreateExtensionDictionary()
ObjectId DBObject.ExtensionDictionary { get; }

parameters.name: ExtensionDictionary
parameters.description: ObjectId.Null when no extension dictionary exists yet.

tools.notes: Empty extension dictionaries add overhead; ReleaseExtensionDictionary removes one that is no longer needed.

tools.name: IExtensionApplication
tools.description: Interface implemented by one class in a .NET plug-in to receive Initialize when the assembly is loaded (NETLOAD or autoloader) and Terminate when AutoCAD shuts down. Used to register event handlers, create UI such as ribbon tabs and palettes, and load settings.
tools.usage:
[assembly: ExtensionApplication(typeof(MyPlugin.App))]
public class App : IExtensionApplication { public void Initialize() {...} public void Terminate() {...} }

parameters.name: Initialize()
parameters.description: Called once on load; keep it fast and exception-safe.

parameters.name: Terminate()
parameters.description: Called on AutoCAD shutdown only; .NET assemblies cannot be unloaded.

parameters.name: [assembly: CommandClass]
parameters.description: Companion attribute naming the classes that contain [CommandMethod]s, which speeds loading.

tools.notes: Exceptions thrown in Initialize are swallowed or shown as load errors; wrap the body in try/catch and log. Ribbon creation should wait for the ribbon to exist (ComponentManager.ItemInitialized).

tools.name: CommandFlags
tools.description: Flags passed to [CommandMethod] that control how a .NET command runs: modal or transparent, whether it uses the pickfirst set, whether it runs in session context, where it is allowed, and undo behaviour.
tools.usage: [CommandMethod("GROUP", "GLOBALNAME", "LOCALNAME", CommandFlags.Modal | CommandFlags.UsePickSet)]

parameters.name: Modal / Transparent
parameters.description: Modal (default) cannot run inside another command; Transparent can (prefix ' when invoked).

parameters.name: UsePickSet / Redraw
parameters.description: Access the pickfirst set; keep grips/selection after the command.

parameters.name: Session
parameters.description: Run in application context, required for switching or opening documents.

parameters.name: NoPaperSpace / NoTileMode / NoBlockEditor / NoUndoMarker / NoHistory
parameters.description: Restrictions on where the command may run and how it is recorded.

tools.example:
[CommandMethod("ACME", "RENUM", "RENUM", CommandFlags.Modal | CommandFlags.UsePickSet | CommandFlags.NoBlockEditor)]
public void Renumber() { /* ... */ }
tools.notes: Session commands must lock documents themselves (Document.LockDocument) before modifying them.

tools.name: PackageContents.xml
tools.description: The manifest of an Autodesk application bundle (a folder named *.bundle) used by the AutoCAD autoloader to load .NET assemblies, ObjectARX modules, LISP files and partial CUIx files automatically, per AutoCAD version, without NETLOAD or acad.lsp edits.
tools.usage:
%APPDATA%\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins\Acme.bundle\PackageContents.xml
%PROGRAMDATA%\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins\  or  %PROGRAMFILES%\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins\

parameters.name: ApplicationPackage
parameters.description: Root element: SchemaVersion, AutodeskProduct="AutoCAD", Name, AppVersion, ProductCode (GUID).

parameters.name: Components / RuntimeRequirements
parameters.description: OS="Win64", Platform="AutoCAD*", SeriesMin/SeriesMax such as R25.0 (2025) and R25.1 (2026); set SeriesMax for .NET 8 vs .NET Framework builds.

parameters.name: ComponentEntry
parameters.description: AppName, ModuleName="./Contents/Acme.dll" (.dll, .arx/.dbx, .lsp/.fas/.vlx or .cuix module), LoadOnAutoCADStartup or LoadOnCommandInvocation with a Commands list.

tools.example:
<ApplicationPackage SchemaVersion="1.0" AutodeskProduct="AutoCAD" Name="Acme Tools" AppVersion="1.2.0" ProductCode="{8C2A...}">
  <Components>
    <RuntimeRequirements OS="Win64" Platform="AutoCAD*" SeriesMin="R25.0" SeriesMax="R25.1" />
    <ComponentEntry AppName="AcmeTools" ModuleName="./Contents/2025/Acme.dll" LoadOnAutoCADStartup="True" />
  </Components>
</ApplicationPackage>
tools.notes: APPAUTOLOAD controls when bundles load; trusted locations and SECURELOAD still apply. AutoCAD 2025 switched to .NET 8, so ship separate assemblies for 2024-and-earlier and bound them with SeriesMin/SeriesMax.

tools.name: Database.ReadDwgFile
tools.description: Reads a DWG file into a side database that is not open in the editor, the fastest way to query or modify many drawings (batch attribute extraction, block import, title-block updates) without the overhead of opening documents.
tools.usage:
var sideDb = new Database(false, true);
sideDb.ReadDwgFile(string fileName, FileOpenMode mode, bool allowCPConversion, string password);

parameters.name: new Database(false, true)
parameters.description: buildDefaultDrawing = false, noDocument = true: required for reading an existing file.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: FileOpenMode.OpenForReadAndAllShare, OpenForReadAndWriteNoShare, OpenForReadAndReadShare, OpenTryForReadShare.

parameters.name: allowCPConversion
parameters.description: Allow code-page conversion for legacy drawings.

tools.notes: Some operations (text alignment, attribute AdjustAlignment, certain regens) need HostApplicationServices.WorkingDatabase temporarily set to the side database. Cannot read a file that is open for write by another user when a write mode is requested.

tools.name: Database.SaveAs
tools.description: Saves a database (side database or a document's database) to a DWG file in a chosen format version. DxfOut writes DXF. Used in batch processing and for down-saving to older releases.
tools.usage:
void Database.SaveAs(string fileName, DwgVersion version)
void Database.SaveAs(string fileName, bool bBakAndRename, DwgVersion version, SecurityParameters security)
void Database.DxfOut(string fileName, int precision, DwgVersion version)

parameters.name: bBakAndRename
parameters.description: Create a .bak of the existing file first.

parameters.name: precision
parameters.description: DxfOut decimal places (0-16).

tools.notes: Saving the active document's database with SaveAs does not rename the document in the editor; use the document-level save commands for that. Enum names follow internal version codes rather than release years.

tools.name: Database.WblockCloneObjects
tools.description: Copies objects from one database to another, with all their dependencies (layers, linetypes, styles, nested blocks). It is the standard way to import block definitions, layers or styles from a library drawing into the current drawing.
tools.usage: void Database.WblockCloneObjects(ObjectIdCollection ids, ObjectId ownerId, IdMapping mapping, DuplicateRecordCloning cloning, bool deferTranslation)

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Objects in the source database to copy.

parameters.name: ownerId
parameters.description: Owner in the destination, e.g. destination BlockTableId for block definitions.

parameters.name: cloning
parameters.description: DuplicateRecordCloning.Ignore (keep existing), Replace (redefine), MangleName.

tools.notes: Call it outside any open transaction on the destination objects involved, or at least with the owner closed. The IdMapping maps source ids to new ids afterwards.

tools.name: HostApplicationServices.WorkingDatabase
tools.description: Static property holding the database that AutoCAD treats as current for operations that implicitly use 'the' database, such as SetDatabaseDefaults, text alignment and some entity constructors. Normally the active document's database; temporarily switched when working on side databases.
tools.usage: Database HostApplicationServices.WorkingDatabase { get; set; }

parameters.name: set
parameters.description: Assign a side database temporarily; always restore the previous value in finally.

tools.notes: In accoreconsole and Design Automation this is the drawing loaded with /i. Leaving a side database as working database after it is disposed crashes AutoCAD.
